_about: Config for the career-engine pipeline. 'database_backend' names your tracker (default 'notion'). REQUIRED keys (a run stops without them): output_folder, and database_id (only when a database backend is configured). EVERY other key is OPTIONAL — pipelines run without it and an optional key that is missing or empty simply means the plugin's own defaults apply (role_matching, cv_title_rules and scope_preferences in particular are never reported as missing), so an older config never breaks. View URL keys (database_*_view_url) are optional fast-paths: when present, the pipeline skips the 59KB Notion database discovery fetch and queries the view directly. Legacy names (notion_database_id, notion_needs_editing_view_url, notion_property, idea_bank.notion_database_id, idea_bank.notion_page_url) are still read for backward compatibility; prefer the database_* names. This file is the single source of truth for job-search preferences: target_titles through screening_answers below replace the retired references/job-preferences.md and source-open-roles' own ~/.career-engine-job-prefs.json — there is no other preferences store. There is no `cv_template` or `word_templates_path` key — CV/cover-letter/Hebrew templates resolve by fixed filename convention from `references/templates/` inside career-data (`cv.dotx`, `cover-letter-template.dotx`, `cvHe.dotm`, `he-letter.dotx`); the plugin never reads a config key or an external OS path for them.

cv_type.description: Which CV format to produce. 'Detailed' (default) = the existing full CV. 'Brief' = the one-page two-column condensed CV. 'Variant' = read the per-role 'CV Type' field from your configured database backend instead (values 'Detailed'/'Brief') — defaults to Detailed if that field is empty for a role; under Variant the career coach recommends a value at intake and fills the field only when empty (your own value always wins). The 'CV Type' database field is a fixed name — setup instructs you to add it directly. brief_has_photo ('yes'/'no', optional) tells cv-writer whether your Brief template has a photo — leave blank to assume no photo. market_norms (optional free text) = YOUR OWN CV-format norms per market, e.g. 'Israeli tech: Brief unless C-suite; US roles: Detailed' — when present, it is the authoritative first source for the coach's CV Type recommendation.

cv_footer.description: Whether the user wants to inject their Education and Languages as part of the workflow. If not, the user needs to inject themselves after the workflow ends.

role_matching_description: OPTIONAL. How roles are matched to you. 'capabilities' (default when absent) = responsibility coverage against your capability profile and background, titles only a nudge — sourcing, Prioritization and the coach all score what a role asks you to do. 'titles' = rigid, official-titles-only: Prioritization uses the title-based read, sourcing keeps the title rubric, and the CV plan defaults to Keep (your recorded titles).

scope_preferences.description: OPTIONAL. Responsibilities you want more of (want) and refuse to do (avoid), in generic discipline vocabulary (e.g. 'category creation', 'sales-quota ownership'). Feeds matching only: sourcing, Prioritization and the coach's Priority. Never a hard filter and never a run blocker.

cv_title_rules_description: OPTIONAL. Standing CV-title rules, replacing the per-role 'CV Title Preferences' tracker field (still read when present). Each entry: {"employer": "", "disposition": "keep|retitle-as", "title": "", "note": ""}. Feeds presentation only: the coach's CV Titles plan and the cv-writer.

title_variants.description: Search variant sets per target title, ~6-8 each (seniority variants like Lead/Manager/Director/Head/VP, phrasing variants like PMM/Product Marketing Manager, adjacent-function variants). Keys are your target titles; values are arrays of variant strings searched at sourcing time. Example: {"Head of Marketing": ["VP Marketing", "Marketing Director", "Head of Growth", "GTM Lead"]}. Seeded on first sourcing run if empty; human-editable any time.

industry_fit.description: Domains to prioritize (high), consider (medium), or deprioritize (low) when sourcing and scoring roles. All optional; nothing currently enforces these as hard filters — the coach reads them as context.

company_stage_fit.description: Company stages (e.g. Seed, Series A/B/C, Public, PE-backed) to prioritize, consider, or deprioritize. Advisory context for the coach, not a hard filter.

employment_type_preference.description: Employment types to seek, accept, or exclude by default (e.g. contract-to-hire acceptable; pure contract, freelance, part-time, fractional excluded unless requested in a session).

screening_answers.description: Your standing answers to common screening questions. Intake flags a conflict OR confirms a match in Patterns; sourcing down-ranks a conflicting role with a visible label. Free text; leave any field blank to skip it (e.g. travel: 'open to frequent travel' or 'prefer minimal travel'). compensation_floor also serves as the sourcing scoring rubric's salary floor — there is no separate min-salary field.

idea_bank.description: Database for idea capture (mind-dump pipeline). Set database_id to your Ideas database ID.

linkedin_post.description: LinkedIn post writing pipeline config. default_format_mix is advisory for the content orchestrator.

content_calendar.description: Content calendar orchestrator config. default_batch_size is the number of posts per orchestrator run.

pricing_floors.description: Your minimum prices (the agent never quotes below these in copy). fiverr_basic/standard/premium are the three Fiverr gig-tier floors; upwork_hourly is your Upwork hourly-rate floor (net — list rate is this divided by 0.8 to absorb Upwork's 20% cut). Leave any field blank to skip it.

freelance.description: Freelance-manager config (Fiverr + Upwork). fiverr_username, upwork_profile_url, and brand_name are platform handles; pricing_floors holds your minimum prices. All optional — the freelance-manager asks inline for anything blank.
